chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Khurrazād, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Rāshid, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Abī Saʿīd, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “If a woman dies among a group of people among whom she has no maḥram, they pour water over her. And if a man dies among women among whom he has no maḥram...”
Then Abū Ḥanīfah said: “They should pour water over him.”

So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Rather, it is permissible for them to touch of him whatever it was permissible for them to look at of him while he was alive. Then when they reach the place at which it was not permissible for them to look while he was alive, nor to touch it, they should pour water over him.”

key_terms.الْمَوْضِعَ: the bodily area or part in question
key_terms.ذَاتُ مَحْرَمٍ: a female maḥram relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a maḥram relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.يَصُبُّونَ: they pour water over the body

ai.seo_question: How should the body of a deceased man or woman be washed if no maḥram is present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about washing the deceased when no maḥram is present. It distinguishes between areas of the body that were ordinarily permissible to see and touch during life and those that were not, instructing direct contact only in the former and pouring water without touch for the latter.
